events.note: Authored for credential-evidence epic #238 (Group E follow-up) from the contract claims and handoffs E1, E2 and E3 cited in the expectation, before any scanner was consulted; carrier existence is provider-documented, the context policy is project policy. Not an independent review.

Decided 2026-10-06 by the sole maintainer (Milo Kang, milocosmopolitan, repository owner) for credential-evidence epic #238 (Group E follow-up), on the owner's instruction of 2026-10-06 (complete redact-secret#1228, #1229 and #1230 before the next release; Cases and baselines authored maintainer-only, as in Batch 2). No dissent was raised by the maintainer; the strongest counter-argument is recorded in the dissent field. Question: A value in the api_key URL parameter of an Airtable request is a credential whatever its shape and whether or not the key's end date has passed? Options: leave the case a draft because the only mention of the parameter is a negative sentence in a current page; require a documented key format (none is stated); or flag by position and not by era. Decision: flag any value in the api_key URL parameter of an Airtable API request, with no era exception. Reason: Airtable names the parameter as the legacy key's carrier and describes the key as all-or-nothing account access, but states no value format and no statement settles whether a key authenticated after 2024-02-01, so the expectation rests on project policy and is not a provider rule; a retired key in a URL is still a redaction concern. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone under the solo-maintainer period (ADR 0020): not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). Recorded by an AI agent on the owner's instruction.
events.dissent: The page names the parameter only to say it is not supported for tokens, so it may not describe how keys were presented; a generic api_key parameter also appears in unrelated services, so a position rule can flag non-Airtable values; and the keys were switched off, so the redaction may protect nothing; leaving the case a draft would claim nothing.
events.reversingEvidence: A pinned capture of the pre-2023 Airtable API reference showing a different presentation form, or an Airtable statement of the key format or confidentiality that contradicts this outcome, or a second maintainer's retro-review that disputes it.
